species_support: human and mouse VEGF-D receptor-specificity assays
evidence_summary: Primary receptor-binding and cross-linking studies identify VEGFR2/KDR and VEGFR3/FLT4 as VEGF-D receptors and report that VEGF-D does not bind VEGFR1/FLT1 under the tested conditions.
limitations: Retain mature VEGFD-KDR/FLT4 receptor and species boundaries; do not transfer VEGF-A/FLT1 specificity to VEGF-D or infer an FLT1 route from VEGF-family membership.

species_support: human and mouse VEGF/VEGF-D endothelial and integrin studies
evidence_summary: Primary studies support VEGF-family cooperation with integrin-mediated endothelial migration and signaling, and directly identify alpha9beta1 as a binding partner for VEGF-A/C/D, but they do not establish VEGFD binding to the listed alpha1, alpha2, alpha4 or alpha5 integrins.
limitations: Retain VEGFD-KDR/FLT4 and integrin-assisted endothelial signaling as separate contextual layers; require an exact VEGFD-to-integrin binding or receptor-dependent assay before promotion and do not transfer alpha9beta1 evidence across integrin subunits.
